ios.desc:
Find IT and software developer jobs in Switzerland with salary ranges listed upfront. SwissDevJobs helps you compare pay, technologies and locations before you apply.

Browse roles in software engineering, DevOps, data, cybersecurity, testing and IT support. Open an offer to read the responsibilities, required skills and benefits. Check each offer for remote or hybrid working arrangements.

Search filters
Set a minimum salary and filter by location, technologies, experience, job type, company size and company type. You can also select the language required for the role.

Locations and employers
Browse jobs alongside their locations on the map in landscape or on a wider screen. Explore company profiles to learn more about employers and their tech stacks.

Saved jobs and applications
Save jobs to return to later. When you are ready to apply, open the application page from the offer.

Salary statistics
Compare salary statistics by technology, city and experience level. Browse local tech communities and events to stay connected with the Swiss IT industry.

show_hn.title: Show HN: I built a Flutter job app for both Android and iOS

quotes.text:
I've built a Flutter app.

With not much prior experience (my first big development project), I somehow managed to pull this off. The whole process took about 5 months, mainly coding on weekends and late nights. The app is built upon SwissDevJobs' API and is available on both mobile platforms. The entire deployment process went smoothly. I had heard many horror stories about the App Store and its strict review procedure, but my app was accepted on the first try, so I guess there's nothing to be afraid of :)

Here are some "technical" details and my observations:
It wouldn't have been possible to build this without the support of the entire Flutter community and third-party packages. Many essential functionalities are missing in the framework itself. Otherwise, you'd find yourself delving into the dark void of native code. State management is pretty much non-existent, so you need to rely on external solutions - for me, it was Provider.
Many people might initially be thrown off by the way Flutter uses endless nested widget trees. Trust me, after a few days, you'll fall in love with this approach. It's intuitive and pleasant to work with.
Dart is one of the best languages out there. I've tried many of them, perhaps too many, and Dart easily ranks as one of my all-time favorites. It's clean, intuitive, and I hope it will gain more popularity beyond just being used in Flutter.

Check it out, and please share your thoughts. Happy to hear all feedback, so don't hold back. Any …
